description: DISPATCH-STALL-ALERT (docs/operations/aws-revisao-arquitetura.md, finding 32): how long, in seconds, a job that a dispatcher would start now (a first candidate of its queue whose route has a free slot it may take) may stay queued before a service process that stands by alerts (platform.dispatch.stalled, published to the platform's topic once when it starts and once when it ends). A live dispatcher starts such a job on its next tick (service.dispatch_s, 1 s), and a service that takes the role over does it within seconds of the swap or of a failover (deploy.live_stale_s, 10 s); 120 s is past every one of those and well under the 7.7 minutes of 11/11 with no dispatch and no alert.
